sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Virginia, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 23Passed

Your application must reach your local general registrar by 5 p.m. on the eleventh day before the election: Friday, October 23, 2026. (the law)

Send it back

Hand-delivered and drop-off ballots must reach your general registrar's office by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A mailed ballot counts if it is postmarked on or before Election Day and reaches the registrar's office by noon on the third day after the election: Friday, November 6, 2026. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Virginia’s own site

At school away from home, in Virginia or in another state? What Virginia says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered voter can apply to vote absentee by mail, either for the next election or for all future elections by joining the permanent absentee list. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply on the Department of Elections' Citizen Portal ("Apply to Vote Absentee by Mail"). You give your name, date of birth, the last four digits of your Social Security number, and your driver's license or state ID number. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Download the absentee application (English, Spanish, Vietnamese or Korean), fill it in and sign it, and send it to your local general registrar's office by mail, fax, or as a scanned attachment to an email. Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can fill out a paper application at your local general registrar's office. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the postage-paid return envelope. It must be postmarked by Election Day and arrive by noon on Friday, November 6. A commercial delivery service counts as mail; a private courier or another person does not. (the law)
  • Drop box. Take it to a drop-off location in your county or city by 7 p.m. on Election Day. The instructions mailed with your ballot list the drop-off sites; your local registrar's office can also tell you. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it yourself to your local general registrar's office by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)

What the envelope needs

No witness is needed. Seal your ballot in the envelope provided and fill in and sign the Statement of Voter on the back: your full name, your Virginia home address, your signature, the last four digits of your Social Security number, and your birth year. Leaving off your middle name or the date does not void your ballot. Some voters who registered by mail and are voting in a federal election for the first time will get a notice asking them to include a copy of an ID (such as a photo ID, or a utility bill or bank statement showing name and address). (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Virginia’s own site

Track a mailed ballot on Ballot Scout, or check on the Citizen Portal whether your application was received and your ballot sent and received. Voters in Fairfax County and Prince William County use their counties' own trackers. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Friday, September 18, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Early voting in person runs from Friday, September 18 through 5 p.m. Saturday, October 31, 2026, at your local registrar's office and any satellite sites. No reason or application is needed. Offices are also open on Sunday, October 18, Saturday, October 24, Sunday, October 25 and Saturday, October 31. Bring an accepted ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement. (official page)

Students

At school in Virginia, away from home

Virginia's Department of Elections says a college student may choose to register with their campus address; include your dormitory or residence hall name and its street address, which may differ from your campus mailing address. Your residence for voting is a physical place where you intend to stay for an unlimited time; you can have only one at a time, you declare it yourself, and you may change your intent at any time. Being a student neither counts for nor against living somewhere. A student votes like anyone else: in person, early, or absentee by mail. You must update your registration whenever you change your residence. (official page)

At school in another state, with Virginia as home

The state's pages do not speak to students in other states separately. The State Board's rule is that being a student, or being away as one, does not by itself count for or against where you live. You lose your Virginia voting residence by registering or voting in another county, city or state, and you do not lose your residence at an address until you have set up a residence at another one. A student who keeps a Virginia residence can apply to vote absentee by mail. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application; it must be received by Friday, October 23, 2026 (overseas citizens must also register by then; service members and their families have no registration deadline). A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and received by noon on Friday, November 6, 2026. (federal guide)

Virginia in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to apply for a mailed ballot is this Friday, October 23, 2026, at 5 p.m. Early voting in person continues through Saturday, October 31.
  • If you were hospitalized, fell ill or had another emergency after the deadline, you can ask for an emergency absentee ballot until 2 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026.
  • Voter registration closes Friday, October 23, 2026; after that you can still register and vote a provisional ballot in person through Election Day.
  • Where you live for voting may differ from where you live for taxes, tuition or financial aid; the Department of Elections says to ask the right advisers about those.

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Virginia’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
